segments: "THE PRISONER " in bold white text fades in on a black screen, then quickly fades out
Black screen fades into a scene of outside a cafe. A man wearing a black suit walks up to maid who is cleaning up a table. The maid says "we'll be with you in a minute"
The man reaches for the maid's arm and asks urgently, "Where's the police station?"
Camera cuts to wide shot of the man walking through the street and around the corner while looking for the phone booth. Ominous music plays in the background.
The man walks up to the phone box and grabs an L-shaped phone. He holds it up and examines it
The man begins to walk back towards the camera. He looks around
The man holds his finger up to a screen that says "PUSH AND FIND OUT". Next to it are a large number of black buttons with numbers on them.
A woman wearing a red striped shirt suddenly pulls up in a car

As they're driving, the man asks "why did you speak to me in French?" Woman: "French is international" Man: "I suppose it's a waste of time asking the name of this place" Woman: "as a matter of fact I thought you might be Polish, perhaps a Czech" Man: "What would Poles or Czechs be doing here?" Woman: "It's very cosmopolitan, you never know who you'll meet next"
The woman says "I did tell you we are only local" and the man starts to exit the car
The man looks at a sign in front of the building that says "General Store" before walking in
The man makes eye contact with the clerk, who says "good morning sir, what can I do for you then?" as he walks across the store
The man grabs the book and folds it out on the counter
The man says "I meant a larger map" Clerk: "only in color sir, much more expensive" Man: "that's fine"
The man says "that's not what I meant, I meant a larger area" Clerk: "no we only have local maps sir, there's no demand for any others"
The man says "where can I hired car, self drive?" The clerk says "no self drive, only taxis" The man replies "I've tried those
The clerk walks back across the store, saying "Well I look for the occasional customs sir"
